messages:
alex.w: quick question — i'm poking at the edge routing shape and wondering if we can land on a much smaller decision surface for the common path. current policy graph is powerful but expensive at evaluation time. thoughts on a 'fast path' that does a one-pass resolution for latency-sensitive tenants?
priya: absolutely +1 to a fast path. curious what you mean by "one-pass" — deterministic tie-breaker or heuristic bucket?
sam: idea: do a cheap scoring pass that only considers region, tier, and healthy flag. if result confident (score delta > X) use it. otherwise fall through to full policy. gives most traffic a 2-3x eval speedup.
marta: real question is operator model — how do we guarantee this doesn't change semantics for tenants who rely on complex rules? we need a way to opt-out per-tenant. maybe a config toggle with audit logs.
jin: preemption safety: fast path must respect hard constraints (e.g., tenant.region == eu required, or tenant.sla == gold). soft constraints like cost/affinity can be approximated. otherwise we risk routing to incompatible shapes.
alex.w: agreed. proposal sketch: fast-path checks (all MUST be cheap): region match, tier match, instance healthy, and preemption-safe capacity check. compute a compact key (region:tier:hard-mask) and consult a small cache. only when cache-miss or low-margin do full policy eval.
priya: can we prototype the compact key as a 64-bit fingerprint so cache lookups are atomic? avoids map churn.
sam: yep. cache eviction TTL = 1m by default, plus LRU. also record a confidence score in cache entry (float as string) so we can invalidate entries that show low confidence over time.
marta: telemetry — we need per-route attribution: was chosen by fast-path OR full-eval and reason. also sample reruns of fast-path results through full-eval to detect skew/regressions.
jin: sampling is crucial. pick 1% at first, escalate to 5% if divergence > threshold. that gives us guardrails without huge CPU costs.
alex.w: here's a tiny pseudocode sketch for the fast check:
```
# input: request ctx
key = fingerprint(ctx.region, ctx.tier, ctx.hard_constraints_mask)
entry = fastCache.get(key)
if entry and entry.confidence > 0.85:
  return entry.choice  # immediate route
else:
  return fullPolicyEval(ctx)
```
priya: looks good. how do we generate the hard_constraints_mask? bitfield of required flags? easy to compute for most tenants.
sam: yep bitfield. but watch out for explosion if we include many feature flags. only include constraints that affect compatibility (region required, must-have accelerator, compliance zone).
marta: rollout plan: feature flag gated at tenant-level, start internal-only, 24h shadow, then gradual traffic switch. must include canary in each region.
jin: also need a small validation job that runs nightly to compare fast-path vs full-policy outcomes on a corp-sized sample. alert when divergence > 0.5% for >= 3 days.
alex.w: ops ask: what's the risk to tail latency? fast-path should reduce median/95. if cache misses spike, we could see small blips. mitigation: add jittered backoff and prefer cached soft-fallbacks when backend load is high.
priya: i can prototype the cache and a shim in the router this week. will add metrics: fast_path_hit_ratio, fast_path_confidence_hist, fast_vs_full_divergence.
sam: if you want i can wire a sim harness to replay a day of traffic and show CPU savings and divergence.
marta: add a per-tenant opt-out + admin UI to view fast-path history. ops will want an override to disable for a tenant on incidents.
alex.w: decision items summary: 1) implement compact-key fast-cache with confidence + TTL, 2) enforce hard-constraints in fast-path, 3) 1% sampling to full-eval initially, 4) per-tenant opt-out flag + audit logs, 5) nightly divergence job + alerts, 6) rollout plan (internal shadow -> canary -> gradual).
jin: we should also document which policy primitives are "fast-safe" vs "full-only" (e.g., hard region/tier = safe; custom scoring functions = full-only).
priya: noted. i'll make a short RFC PR outlining primitives and the shim API.
deploy-bot: deploy pending: alex/fast-path-shim branch -> staging (pipeline queued) :rocket:
alex.w: thanks all — i'll file the RFC PR and link here. ping me if you want to be reviewer. :)
